content: Did anyone make a handy way to find all structures that extend a certain structure? Especially for classes, since the instance list on the documentation page doesn't list subclass instances.

My attempt:

import Mathlib
open Lean

def Lean.Expr.getForallBinderTypes : Expr → List Expr
  | forallE _ type body _ => type :: body.getForallBinderTypes
  | _ => []

run_cmd
  let env ← getEnv
  for (name, info) in env.constants.map₁ do
    match info with
    | .inductInfo inductVal =>
      for ctorName in inductVal.ctors do
        let .some <| .ctorInfo ctorVal := env.find? ctorName | continue
        for arg in ctorVal.type.getForallBinderTypes do
          let .const argName _ := arg.getAppFn | continue
          let .some <| .inductInfo _ := env.find? argName | continue -- verify it is a structure
            logInfo m!"{name} extends {argName}"
    | .defnInfo defnVal =>
      -- handle "inlined" dependencies (such as "Field extends DivisionRing") by going over defs as well
      if name.lastComponentAsString.startsWith "to" then
        let .some arg := defnVal.type.getForallBinderTypes.getLast? | continue
        let .const argName _ := arg.getAppFn | continue
        let .const resultName _ := defnVal.type.getForallBody.getAppFn | continue
        let .some <| .inductInfo _ := env.find? argName | continue -- verify the arg is a structure
        let .some <| .inductInfo _ := env.find? resultName | continue -- verify the result is a structure
        logInfo m!"{argName} extends {resultName}"
    | _ => continue

This is an over-estimate as it doesn't distinguish between extends / fields / instance arguments / manually created defs that begin with "to". I believe the only way to make it miss an implication is by renaming parent projections to not start with "to", but probably nobody does that. But I'm new to metaprogramming so I might be missing stuff.

So I believe if you take the transitive closure of it (e.g. using Python's networkx, or maybe functions from ImportGraph) you'll be able to find all "subclasses" as you asked for.

Update:

Updated code

import Mathlib
open Lean

def Lean.Expr.getForallBinderTypes : Expr → List Expr
  | forallE _ type body _ => type :: body.getForallBinderTypes
  | _ => []

def Lean.Expr.getSelfForallBinderType : Expr → Option Expr
  | forallE currentName type body _ =>
    -- make sure to get the innermost arg in case there are multiple `self`s
    body.getSelfForallBinderType.or <| if currentName == `self then type else none
  | _ => none

def depsFromDecl (env : Environment) (name : Name) (info : ConstantInfo) : List <| Name × Name := do
  match info with
  | .inductInfo inductVal =>
    inductVal.ctors.flatMap fun ctorName ↦
      match env.find? ctorName with
      | .some <| .ctorInfo ctorVal =>
        ctorVal.type.getForallBinderTypes.flatMap fun arg ↦
          match arg.getAppFn with
          | .const argName _ =>
            match env.find? argName with -- verify it is a structure
            | .some <| .inductInfo _ =>
              [(argName, name)]
            | _ => []
          | _ => []
      | _ => []
  | .defnInfo defnVal =>
    -- handle "inlined" dependencies (such as "Field extends DivisionRing") by going over defs as well
    if not <| name.lastComponentAsString.startsWith "to" then [] else
      match defnVal.type.getSelfForallBinderType with
      | .some arg =>
        match arg.getAppFn, defnVal.type.getForallBody.getAppFn with
        | .const argName _, .const resultName _ =>
          match env.find? argName, env.find? resultName with -- verify these are structures
          | .some <| .inductInfo _, .some <| .inductInfo _ =>
            [(resultName, argName)]
          | _, _ => []
        | _, _ => []
      | _ => []
  | _ => []

def depsFromEnv (env : Environment) : NameMap <| Array Name :=
  env.constants.map₁.fold (init := ∅) fun map name info ↦
    depsFromDecl env name info |>.foldl (init := map) fun map (baseClass, subClass) ↦
      map.insert baseClass <| map.getD baseClass #[] |>.push subClass

run_cmd
  let baseClass := ``DivisionRing
  let env ← getEnv
  let deps := depsFromEnv env
  let refs := deps.getD baseClass #[] |>.sortDedup (ord := ⟨Name.cmp⟩)
  let := MessageData.joinSep (refs.toList.map (m!"  {Expr.const · []}")) m!"\n"
  logInfo m!"Found {refs.size} structures that depend on {Expr.const baseClass []}:\n{this}"

Removed some false positives, and refactored to have a "graph" we can query and take the transitive closure of.
Sadly calling deps.transitiveClosure makes Lean crash with a stack overflow, but I think it's great as a prototype. I guess we could DFS/BFS when querying instead of transitive closure.

The code above finds 10 structures that depend on DivisionRing.

Now supporting transitive lookups

import Mathlib
open Lean

def Lean.Expr.getForallBinderTypes : Expr → List Expr
  | forallE _ type body _ => type :: body.getForallBinderTypes
  | _ => []

def Lean.Expr.getSelfForallBinderType : Expr → Option Expr
  | forallE currentName type body _ =>
    -- make sure to get the innermost arg in case there are multiple `self`s
    body.getSelfForallBinderType.or <| if currentName == `self then type else none
  | _ => none

def depsFromDecl (env : Environment) (name : Name) (info : ConstantInfo) : List <| Name × Name := do
  match info with
  | .inductInfo inductVal =>
    inductVal.ctors.flatMap fun ctorName ↦
      match env.find? ctorName with
      | .some <| .ctorInfo ctorVal =>
        ctorVal.type.getForallBinderTypes.flatMap fun arg ↦
          match arg.getAppFn with
          | .const argName _ =>
            match env.find? argName with -- verify it is a structure
            | .some <| .inductInfo _ =>
              [(argName, name)]
            | _ => []
          | _ => []
      | _ => []
  | .defnInfo defnVal =>
    -- handle "inlined" dependencies (such as "Field extends DivisionRing") by going over defs as well
    if not <| name.lastComponentAsString.startsWith "to" then [] else
      match defnVal.type.getSelfForallBinderType with
      | .some arg =>
        match arg.getAppFn, defnVal.type.getForallBody.getAppFn with
        | .const argName _, .const resultName _ =>
          match env.find? argName, env.find? resultName with -- verify these are structures
          | .some <| .inductInfo _, .some <| .inductInfo _ =>
            [(resultName, argName)]
          | _, _ => []
        | _, _ => []
      | _ => []
  | _ => []

def depsFromEnv (env : Environment) : NameMap <| Array Name :=
  env.constants.map₁.fold (init := ∅) fun map name info ↦
    depsFromDecl env name info |>.foldl (init := map) fun map (baseClass, subClass) ↦
      map.insert baseClass <| map.getD baseClass #[] |>.push subClass

def BFS (graph : NameMap <| Array Name) (s : NameSet) : Elab.Command.CommandElabM NameSet := do
  let mut found : NameSet := ∅
  let mut queue : NameSet := s
  while !queue.isEmpty do
    let current := queue.min!
    queue := queue.erase current
    found := found.insert current
    for neighbor in graph.getD current #[] do
      if !found.contains neighbor then
        queue := queue.insert neighbor
  return found

run_cmd
  -- query:
  let baseClass := ``DivisionRing
  let transitive := true

  let env ← getEnv
  let graph := depsFromEnv env
  let mut results := graph.getD baseClass #[]
  if transitive then
    results := (← BFS graph {baseClass}).toArray
  let refs := results.sortDedup (ord := ⟨Name.quickCmp⟩)
  let := MessageData.joinSep (refs.toList.map (m!"  {Expr.const · []}")) m!"\n"
  logInfo m!"Found {refs.size} structures that depend on {Expr.const baseClass []}:\n{this}"

Finds 164 structures that transitively depend on DivisionRing
docs#Lean.StructureInfo has parentInfo field that is probably more robust way to check relationship than checking for leading "to"
The absence from the instance list should surely be considered a doc-gen bug?
